extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers of Stephen Hawking Fellowship (UKRI/STFC/EPSRC) proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for expert reviewers assessing Stephen Hawking Fellowship proposals submitted to UKRI (STFC/EPSRC). It instructs reviewers on assessment criteria, scoring, ethical/conflict considerations, and how to report strengths/weaknesses and confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Before completing a review please ensure that you do not have a conflict of interest with the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should make themselves familiar with UKRI's conflicts of interest policy (link provided). If a conflict exists, do not review. This protects the organisation and individuals and reduces risk or perception of impropriety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment focuses on ideas not document form
rubrics_metrics.description: You are asked throughout to assess “the proposal” but please be clear that this means the ideas, concepts and approaches contained therein not the specific form of the document itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity of presentation may help or hinder review but is not an assessment criterion; avoid letting elegance of presentation become a competition in stylish writing. Prioritisation meetings find reviews most useful when they explicitly identify main strengths and weaknesses and indicate which are more significant. Raising explicit questions for applicants is helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: COVID-19 related disruption
rubrics_metrics.description: When undertaking your assessment you should consider the unequal impacts that COVID-19 related disruption might have had on the track record and career development of those individuals included in the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the capability of the applicant and their team to deliver the research despite disruption. Consider breaks/delays, disruptive working patterns, loss of ongoing work, role changes; consider unequal impacts on track record rather than penalising applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics (reviewer role)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical considerations should not therefore normally be an assessment criterion and you should not take these into account when making your assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities' ethical approval processes are relied upon. If you have serious personal concern and cannot provide an objective review, decline with reason 'ethical issues'. If the proposal raises ethical issues not clearly identified/addressed, raise these with UKRI for a policy decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web links in the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are not required to consider additional information contained in web links included in the case for support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you choose to view linked material your anonymity to the applicant may be compromised. You may ignore web links without penalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess within the call context
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the proposal within the context of the aims, objectives and specific assessment criteria for that published call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must read the call document (EPSRC/STFC/UKRI call pages) and make their assessment in that context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use journal-based metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: You should not use journal-based metrics, such as journal impact factors, as a surrogate measure of the quality of individual research articles, to assess an investigator’s contributions, or to make funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the value and impact of all research outputs (datasets, software, inventions, patents, preprints, commercial activities, etc.) and a broad range of impact measures including qualitative indicators (influence on policy and practice). Do not use impact factors, conference rankings, H-index or similar when assessing grants; content matters more than journal identity, especially for early-stage investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible working and career breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the unequal impact that flexible working, alternative career routes and career breaks might have had on the track record and career development of those individuals included in the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may cost/tailor support for part-time working and extra costs. Where applicants include flexible working or career break details they need not explain personal circumstances; reviewers should recognise likely effects on productivity and career development and focus on stated impact rather than duration. Flexible working examples are given (reduction in hours, job sharing, compressed hours, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality/Excellence (research quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on the degree of research excellence of the application. Excellence can be characterised by terms such as novel, ambitious, timely, exciting, at the international forefront, adventurous, elegant, or transformative but need not demonstrate all of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a plausible hypothesis with basis in literature and clearly identified objectives. Certainty of outcome is not required; incremental work can still be excellent. Comment on how the application is set in context relative to current state of knowledge and international activity and whether it provides unique UK capability. Reviewers should comment on: an excellent research programme which is novel and timely; a robust methodology appropriate and feasible to attain objectives; a clear vision of contributions and evidence of independence of research ideas. For multidisciplinary applications state which aspects you are qualified to assess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance (research importance/impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on how the proposed research contributes to or helps maintain the health of the research field and addresses key UK societal challenges and economic, social and cultural prosperity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess extent to which research could meet national strategic needs, establish or maintain unique world-leading activity (including niche capability). Evaluate whether potential outcomes are identified and plans for maximising impacts are proportionate, timely and credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant and their development
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how well the proposal demonstrates the candidate’s potential to become a leader in research and public engagement, commensurate with their career stage (post-doctoral).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on: candidate being at post-doctoral stage per call requirements; demonstrated ability to deliver proposed research; a well-considered plan for skills development appropriate to current experience; ability to outline career aspirations and justify why the fellowship route is appropriate. Refer to person specification and fellowship assessment criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the extent to which the candidate evidences history/interest in science communication and public engagement and has plans for development and activities during the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence of previous/current/planned engagement with non-scientific audiences; a clear plan to develop public engagement skills appropriate to experience; demonstration or ambition to be a clear communicator to scientific and non-scientific audiences with methodology and development opportunities; a clear plan for public engagement activities during the Fellowship and how effectiveness will be assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on the effectiveness of proposed planning and management arrangements, and whether requested resources are appropriate and fully justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrangements should be proportionate to scale/complexity. All resources required for the Fellow must be identified and justified. Fellow's direct costs should be included and justified. Comment on suitability of arrangements to access resources other than via the grant (collaborations), viability of arrangements to access equipment (including university/third-party contributions), and identification of risks and appropriateness of contingencies. Assessment should be based solely on resources sought, not derived costs. Note fellowships may be part-time (minimum 50% FTE) and costed accordingly; draw attention to requested items not justified or needed but not identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal research and human participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the proposal involves animal research or human participation comment specifically on ethical considerations and whether ethical approval procedures have been complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on potential adverse consequences for humans, animals or the environment and whether risks have been addressed satisfactorily. For animal research comment specifically on need to use animals, choice of species, and number intended to be used. Resources related to these aspects must be explicitly justified in terms of need, scale and nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers should demonstrate awareness of and commitment to the principles of Responsible Innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsible Innovation promotes creativity and opportunities that are socially desirable and in the public interest; it goes beyond risk/regulation and creates processes to explore purposes, motivations and unpredictable impacts in an open, inclusive and timely way. Reviewers should use the suggested flexible framework steps where appropriate and comment in the Proposal Assessment if a proposal runs counter to these principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall assessment (report to prioritisation panel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overall assessment highlighting strengths and weaknesses identified in individual questions and make a clear and explicit recommendation about whether the proposal warrants funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Quality (excellence) is pre-eminent — no proposal can be funded without clearly demonstrating it. Research Importance should be a major consideration. Weighting between remaining aspects depends on the proposal. Indicate which aspects you accorded higher or lower priority and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score (six-point scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign a score using the six-point scale to reflect your overall conclusion, consistent with comments on individual sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1 = scientifically or technically flawed; 2 = does not meet one or more assessment criteria; 3 = meets all criteria but with clear weaknesses; 4 = good, meets all criteria but with minor weaknesses; 5 = strong, broadly meets all criteria; 6 = very strong, fully meets all criteria. Ensure score aligns with written assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of confidence in the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate your confidence with regard to this review (low, medium or high).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reports your confidence in being able to make the assessment, not your confidence in the proposal's success if funded. If you cannot assess, inform UKRI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expertise and scope of assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: If you can only comment on specific parts of a multidisciplinary or component-based proposal, identify those aspects and give your review on just those aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different reviewers will cover other aspects and the panel will integrate comments. Scores and confidence should reflect only aspects you can assess and you should not moderate them to reflect areas you cannot comment on. Even where you can only comment on one aspect it is helpful to give views on how compelling the arguments for the overall proposal are.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritisation and presentation of strengths/weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews are most useful when they explicitly identify the main strengths and weaknesses, and give a clear view on which should be accorded greater significance and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit questions to applicants are useful. There is no set way to answer the form, but prioritisation panels prefer clear prioritisation and justification of significance.
